clue.text: Maltreat composer's daughter, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words are judged by their sound rather than their spelling

parts.note: the unmarried daughter of the composer Handel would be addressed as Miss Handel

explanation.surface: A cruel act against a famous composer's daughter, reported second-hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Say Miss Handel quickly and you get MISHANDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat roughly or badly is to handle wrongly, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Koala, possibly, is a rum . pal

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters around it are taken in a strange order; the word also lends its own letters

parts.note: every letter of these words, the indicator included, is used

explanation.surface: A koala chum who is a bit of an odd fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is a printing blemish. 'rum' does double duty as indicator and as three of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala carries its young in a pouch, making it one example of a pouched mammal; 'possibly' flags the example.

clue.text: Motionless, lor all thai

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not moving at all

definitions.note: printed garbled; the setter's text was 'for all that'

explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper's scan has garbled 'for all that', which means nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something unmoving and an adverb meaning nevertheless or even so.

clue.text: Proverbial recipient or greater love

parts.note: surface reading: someone in a saying who is loved more deeply
setter's reading: the proverb 'absence makes the heart grow fonder', so the one who is away gets more love

explanation.surface: Who, according to the old saying, is loved the most?
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a misprint for 'of'. The proverb says absence makes the heart grow fonder.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is away is the one whose absence, by the proverb, makes hearts grow fonder of them.

clue.text: Thrice d'Artagnan's role

parts.note: surface reading: a part d'Artagnan played three times, like a recurring stage role
setter's reading: on his first day in Paris d'Artagnan arranged three fights with Athos, Porthos and Aramis

explanation.surface: An actor who has played d'Artagnan three times.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Three Musketeers, d'Artagnan arranges single combats with all three musketeers on the same afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fights formal single combats with swords is the role d'Artagnan took three times over.

clue.text: A dark place, before the subscription was raised

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: sub is the short form of subscription

explanation.surface: A gloomy spot that existed before club fees went up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like a price rise, but in a down answer it means the word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the region of darkness through which the dead pass, a dark place indeed.

clue.text: Odd bachelor at the . dance

parts.note: rum means odd or peculiar
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A strange single man turns up at the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, so the answer names one specific kind.

clue.text: Live with army team

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Someone boarding alongside a military sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell or have one's home somewhere is to live there, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Having a sovereign makes poor Norman fashionable

indicators.note: something in poor shape is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the printed name has a stray final N; the setter's word was the name Norma
chic means stylish

explanation.surface: Turning a struggling Norman into a stylish one gives him a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper printed 'Norman', but only five letters fit, so the intended name was Norma.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchic state is ruled by a king or queen, so it has a crowned head.

clue.text: My poetic claim to be always a ruler?

parts.note: my claim to existence is I am
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, with 'poetic' applying here too

explanation.surface: A poet boasting that he will reign forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'I am e'er', the poet's claim to be always.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, also spelt emir, is a Muslim prince or commander, so a ruler.

clue.text: Note the children send out again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: A note telling the children to go out again.
explanation.definitionFit: To republish or distribute a second time is to send something out once more.

clue.text: Indispensable quality of a German city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: What makes a German city's church special.
explanation.definitionFit: The core nature of a thing, without which it would not be itself, is its indispensable quality.

clue.text: Prussian lancer returns in an infernal hurry

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left
the letters sit inside the following words rather than being built from their meaning

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of infernal and start of hurry

explanation.surface: A cavalryman galloping home in a desperate rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'infernal hurry' sits NALHU; read backwards it is UHLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Uhlans were light cavalry armed with lances in the Prussian and other armies.

clue.text: He washes French and German articles that are in a real mess

indicators.note: the articles sit inside the other letters
a mess is a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: der is the German for the
taken as written
un is the French for a

explanation.surface: A laundryman cleaning up after a jumble of foreign grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: The two articles join into one familiar word, and only 'real' is jumbled; 'a' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cleans clothes and linen is a man who does the washing.

clue.text: Extension of the batsman's position?

wordplay.note: a batsman safely behind the line

explanation.surface: Asking how far the batsman's stance can be widened.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the marked line; a batsman behind it is in the crease and cannot be run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth or enlargement in size or amount is an extension of what was there.

clue.text: Cowardly show by horsemen

parts.note: surface reading: riders putting on a timid display
setter's reading: a cad is a cowardly rogue, whose name ends the word for a mounted procession

explanation.surface: Horsemen giving a spineless display.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a formal procession of riders on horseback, a parade put on by horsemen.

clue.text: Point to Noah's son as being bogus

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
Ham was one of Noah's three sons

explanation.surface: Accusing one of Noah's sons of being a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake, so as an adjective it means false, counterfeit or not genuine.

clue.text: Eddy's Norwegian big brother

parts.note: surface reading: a man called Eddy has an older brother living in Norway
setter's reading: an eddy is a small whirl of water, and its far larger relation is the famous whirlpool off Norway

explanation.surface: Eddy's older sibling, who lives in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moskstraumen off the Lofoten coast of Norway is the original great whirlpool, a giant version of a small swirl of water.

clue.text: Ancient writing decoded from rat.skins'

indicators.note: decoding a message rearranges scrambled symbols into a readable order

parts.note: the stray full stop is a printing blemish

explanation.surface: An old script deciphered from writing on the hides of rats.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the classical language of ancient India, recorded in very old texts.

clue.text: Feelers put out by certain 'workers

parts.note: surface reading: tentative proposals floated by some employees
setter's reading: worker ants, whose heads carry sensory organs

explanation.surface: Some staff sounding out management.
explanation.walkthrough: Feelers can be exploratory approaches; here they are insect organs, and the workers are worker ants.
explanation.definitionFit: The paired sensory organs on an insect's head are literally its feelers.

clue.text: A natural upheaval precedes its downfall

definitions.text: A natural upheaval precedes its downfall

parts.words: A natural upheaval precedes its downfall
parts.note: surface reading: a moral, pride before a fall
setter's reading: a volcanic eruption throws up molten rock which then flows down the slopes

explanation.surface: A proverb-like warning that rising up leads to a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock is thrown up by an eruption and then pours downhill, so the upheaval precedes its flowing down.

clue.text: Bill can't be shaken off, the goose

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who clings and cannot be got rid of, like the shellfish on a hull
second meaning: a species of Arctic goose

explanation.surface: An unwanted Bill, impossible to get rid of, called a silly goose.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hanger-on who sticks fast and a black-and-white Arctic species of wild goose.

clue.text: Lampoon . has one in tears perhaps

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it inside
perhaps signals that the word is only one possible ordering of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mocking sketch that leaves someone crying.
explanation.walkthrough: TEARS rearranged as SATRE holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a piece of mocking ridicule, and a satire is writing that mocks its target.

clue.text: He's comparatively good at the races
Hamlet could only accommodate a few of them

definitions.text: Hamlet could only accommodate a few of them

parts.words: Hamlet could only accommodate a few of them
parts.note: surface reading: Shakespeare's prince could only put up a few guests
setter's reading: a hamlet is a tiny settlement, home to only a handful of residents

explanation.surface: The Prince of Denmark had room for only a few guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The people who live in a small rural settlement are its inhabitants, and a tiny one holds few.

clue.text: Face-saving device has its tips and downs

parts.words: Face-saving device has its tips and downs
parts.note: surface reading: a trick for saving face has its highs and lows
setter's reading: a helmet's face guard literally protects the face and is lifted up and lowered

explanation.surface: A way of avoiding embarrassment that has its ups and downs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' is a misprint for 'ups': the guard is raised and lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable front of a helmet shields the wearer's face, so it is literally a protective guard.

clue.text: Pansy thus calms one's heart?

parts.note: surface reading: a flower soothes someone's feelings
setter's reading: the wild pansy is called heartsease

explanation.surface: A pansy brings comfort to a troubled heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartsease is an old name for the wild pansy; split it as heart's eases.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or relieve pain or worry is to make it lighter, a present-tense verb synonym.

clue.text: 4 might put it up, getting 500 lines

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: rows are lines
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A duellist raises his weapon and is set a punishment of 500 lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 refers to 4-down, DUELLIST. ROWS read upwards is SWOR, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: A duellist raises the blade he fights with, so the weapon is what he might put up.

clue.text: Britain is great? Possibly, in the main

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A patriotic boast questioned: is Britain great, on the whole?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly'; here the main is the sea. Britain is the example of an island ringed by water.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrounded by the sea describes an island set in the main, an old poetic word for the ocean.

clue.text: Private-sounding spite

indicators.note: sounding points to how a word is pronounced rather than how it is written

parts.note: a ranker is a private soldier, from the ranks

explanation.surface: Malice from an enlisted soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A ranker is a soldier serving in the ranks, such as a private; in a British accent it sounds like RANCOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter, long-lasting resentment and malice is spite in a deeper form.

clue.text: See magistrate about a girl

parts.note: re means concerning
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Consult a judge concerning a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or chief magistrate of a town or district in medieval England.

clue.text: The bounder meets mother at the port

parts.note: rotter and bounder are both old slang for a cad
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A cad meets his mother at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam in the Netherlands is one of the largest seaports in Europe.
